evidence: Cic. Par. 49: quam magnum vectīgal sit parsimōnia
terms.comment: From parcō, spare; also written parcimōnia (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plin. Ep. 2.4.3: quod cessat ex reditū, frūgālitāte supplētur
terms.comment: Thrift as a way of life; a thrifty, decent person is frūgī (indeclinable).

terms.gloss: thrifty, frugal; honest, useful (of a person)
terms.grammar: indeclinable adjective (an old dative of frūx); comparative frūgālior, superlative frūgālissimus
evidence: Cic. Deiot. 26: frūgī hominem dīcī nōn multum habet laudis in rēge (Lewis & Short s.v. frūx)
terms.comment: The adjective for “thrifty”. Traupman also gives frūgālis, but Lewis & Short says it is classical only in the comparative and superlative (cf. Quint. 1.6.17); the positive is frūgī.

phrases.latin: Ō dī immortālēs! nōn intellegunt hominēs, quam magnum vectīgal sit parsimōnia.
phrases.english: Good heavens! People don’t understand what a great income thrift is.

phrases.latin: sed quod cessat ex reditū, frūgālitāte supplētur
phrases.english: but whatever my income falls short by is made up by thrift

sources: Lewis & Short: parsimonia · Lewis & Short: frugalitas · Lewis & Short: frugi
